| [THEORY-025](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-025.md) v2 | Neither utility information nor resource holdings, alone or together, can register claims that arise from how differently people convert resources into what they can do and be: equal resources leave unequal capabilities, and utility adapts to deprivation | Sen (1979), [LIT-289](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-289.md), first-hand: a contented disabled person has no marginal-utility claim, no total-utility deficit and no primary-goods deficit, yet an evident claim. | [THEORY-137](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-137.md) v2 | Attributions of mental states to institutions, such as the knowledge that the collective knowledge doctrine of corporate criminal law attributes to a corporation no member of which held it, work largely by shaping the institutions to which they are made rather than by describing states they already had: the attribution holds the institution to a norm, the institution builds structures to meet it, and it becomes more predictable from the intentional stance, whether or not institutions really have minds | Tollefsen (2025), [LIT-736](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-736.md). | [THEORY-140](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-140.md) v2 | The Columbia Accident Investigation Board found that the institutional causes of the Challenger accident had not been fixed and recurred in Columbia's: in both, evidence that the design was not performing as expected was repeatedly reinterpreted as acceptable, each decision seeming correct in itself and each survived anomaly justifying the next flight, while budget and schedule pressure, consensus sign-off, a hierarchy that kept dissent from rising and a safety organization dependent on the program it oversaw sustained the pattern for twenty years and undid post-Challenger reforms | Columbia Accident Investigation Board (2003), [LIT-734](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-734.md), applying Vaughan's normalization of deviance ([LIT-715](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-715.md), unread). | [THEORY-144](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-144.md) | Under steady cost and effort pressure, an organization's activity migrates toward the boundary of acceptable performance, and redundant defences erode unobserved because a breach of one shows no effect, so that major accidents arise from many locally reasonable decisions rather than from coincident errors | Rasmussen (1997), [LIT-743](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-743.md). Within a work space bounded by functional, administrative and safety constraints, a cost gradient from management and an effort gradient from the work drive activity toward the boundary. | [THEORY-149](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-149.md) | Users can govern a shared resource durably without either privatisation or central control, and the institutions that last are marked not by particular rules but by structural regularities: user-made and user-monitored rules, graduated sanctions, cheap local conflict resolution, recognised rights to self-organise, and nested layers of governance | Ostrom's account, read in her Nobel lecture ([LIT-719](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-719.md)). Coded case meta-analyses, laboratory and field experiments and multi-country field studies agree that resource users often self-govern successfully. | [THEORY-150](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-150.md) | A platform that sits between the two sides of a market and can cheaply change how it allocates value tends to decay in three stages, first good to its users, then abusing them to favour its business customers, then abusing both to claw the value back for itself, each stage made possible by the lock-in the one before it built; how far it can go is set by the cost of leaving, so lowering that cost is the remedy | Doctorow's enshittification, as he states it in the 2023 essay that named it, [LIT-731](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-731.md). | [THEORY-152](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-152.md) | When a firm, public service or other organization deteriorates, its members' exit and voice are both recuperation mechanisms: voice carries richer information than exit and can be felt as a benefit rather than a cost, exit can be costly even without loyalty and can signal nothing, loyalty makes members voice rather than exit, and an organization needs floor levels of both for feedback but disintegrates or is disrupted beyond ceiling levels, while its managers may favour whichever response least threatens their hold on power | Hirschman (1974; Milbank reprint 1980), [LIT-750](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-750.md), revisiting his 1970 book ([LIT-748](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-748.md), unread). | [THEORY-153](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-153.md) | A system can keep its identity independently within a shared environment only if it has five interacting subsystems, the first made of elements that are themselves viable systems, so that the structure recurs at every level of recursion; when one is missing or fails, the system degrades in characteristic ways, and without the subsystem for foresight the subsystems for operational control and for identity collapse into each other, leaving a system that can only react | Beer's Viable System Model, as he states it in his 1984 retrospective [LIT-752](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-752.md). | [THEORY-173](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-173.md) v2 | Large models are a cultural and social technology rather than agents: lossy, uninvertible summaries of human-produced information that, like prices and bureaucratic categories, let it be reorganized at scale | Farrell, Gopnik, Shalizi & Evans (2025), [LIT-848](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-848.md), read in [NOTE-649](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-649.md). | [THEORY-207](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-207.md) v2 | Responsibility for a morally loaded outcome that emerges from morally neutral interactions in a network of agents can be allocated without fault or intention, by default and overridably, in full to every causally accountable node, and a rule so allocating it, made common knowledge, works as a corrective that prevents such outcomes | Floridi (2016), [LIT-899](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-899.md), read in [NOTE-699](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-699.md). | [THEORY-218](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-218.md) v2 | In one case study of the 2017 r/place Mona Lisa, what was added to or removed from the image was, once its forum opened, decided off the canvas, in a forum of 161 accounts negotiating through linked design images, where a few central members admitted or refused additions, and the forum's changes then appeared in a region where about 77,000 accounts placed tiles, most of whom never posted; how many placers followed the designs is not measured, and the authors argue that the placement record alone cannot show who directed the image or who cooperated | Litherland & Mørch (2021), [LIT-1037](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1037.md), read in [NOTE-733](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-733.md). | [THEORY-219](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-219.md) v2 | Agency in the sense that bears on responsibility needs a standpoint that settles and carries forward revised evaluative standards when its inherited ones break down, and planning, autonomy, memory and coordination do not supply one | Kahl (2026), [LIT-1033](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1033.md), read in [NOTE-723](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-723.md). | [THEORY-223](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-223.md) | When the rules that govern a system lie within its own action space, the governor's authority rests on the system leaving them alone, and further controls in the same space inherit that dependence | Lahiri (2026), [LIT-1039](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1039.md), read in [NOTE-732](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-732.md). | [THEORY-327](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-327.md) v2 | Fricker, in her 2003 paper and her 2017 retrospective, holds that testimonial injustice is an ingenuous misjudgement of a speaker's credibility caused by prejudice, and that deliberate manipulation of credibility is a related but distinct wrong; and she accepts Anderson's structural form, which is pre-emptive: a speaker's word is never sought because of a structural prejudice, such as an un-refreshed list, that is no one's fault | Fricker, in her own words, in two papers read in full: the paper that introduced testimonial injustice (2003, [LIT-1049](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1049.md), [NOTE-860](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-860.md)), and her retrospective chapter (2017, [LIT-1048](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1048.md), [NOTE-853](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-853.md)). | [THEORY-450](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-450.md) | Across 1,176 premodern archaeological sites, the house-size Gini rises only weakly with the number of levels of political hierarchy and with polity population, and the spread of Gini widens with scale: scale raises the ceiling on domestic wealth inequality without setting its level | Feinman et al.
